scene.speaker: tomas
scene.bubble: Head, arms, legs, feet — my body loves to MOVE! Ready for body gymnastics?
scene.intro: Tomás cannot sit still today! He has got two arms, two legs, two feet and one very fast body — and he wants to move all of them. Head, arms, hands, legs, feet: he touches them one by one and then jumps up again. Pip has got two little wings and one orange beak, so he tries the game too. What have YOU got? Touch your head, touch your nose, and let's move with Tomás!

words.clue: It is between your shoulder and your hand.
You walk and run with it.
You put a shoe on it.

activities.title: Match the body part with what it does.
Listen to body gymnastics. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.script: Tomas: Body gymnastics! Touch your head with two hands. … Freya: Done! This is easy. … Tomas: Now stand on one leg. One, two, three… … Freya: I'm a flamingo! … Tomas: Clap your hands five times! … Freya: One, two, three, four, five! … Tomas: Now touch your toes… and jump like Pip! … Freya: Pip doesn't jump, he flies! … Tomas: Then flap your arms! Great gymnastics, team!

activities.title: Quick check · Choose the correct word.

data.text: Play Touch: say a body part, your partner touches it fast ("Touch your knee!"). Five each — faster every time!

activities.title: Two pictures, many differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 12 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Draw yourself and label 6 body parts. Write: I have got two arms…

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.
